items.sum: The Minister of Indigenous Services announced $1.55 billion in federal funding to renew Jordan's Principle through March 31, 2027. The funding supports continued access to essential services for children.

items.title: Minister announces update on Jordan's Principle
items.sum: Minister of Indigenous Services Mandy Gull-Masty will hold a press conference to provide an update on Jordan's Principle, a policy addressing inequities in government services for Indigenous children.

items.title: Prime Minister Carney to diversify Canada’s trade, attract new investment, and secure new partnerships with visits to India, Australia, and Japan - pm.gc.ca

items.title: Minister announces new investments for Inuit communities
items.sum: Minister of Indigenous Services Mandy Gull-Masty announced new investments to support Inuit children and families, strengthen community well-being, and improve food security across Inuit Nunangat. The announcement was made in Kuujjuaq with Makivvik Executives.

items.title: Immigration minister outlines 2026 Express Entry talent priorities
items.sum: The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship delivered remarks on how Canada's Express Entry system will prioritize skilled workers in 2026. Express Entry is the federal program for selecting economic immigrants based on qualifications and work experience.

items.title: Canada adjusts immigration to address labour shortages
items.sum: The government is using immigration to fill labour gaps in priority industries where domestic workers are unavailable. This approach is intended to support economic resilience and growth.

items.title: Canada adjusts Express Entry immigration categories for 2026
items.sum: Canada is modifying its Express Entry immigration system to attract highly skilled workers while aiming for more sustainable immigration levels. The changes are part of a strategy to compete globally for talent while supporting economic needs.

items.title: Minister announces support measures for Inuit communities
items.sum: Minister of Indigenous Services Mandy Gull-Masty will announce initiatives to support Inuit communities in Inuit Nunangat. The announcement will take place at a quarterly meeting of the Kativik Regional Government.

items.title: Immigration minister to announce Express Entry category changes
items.sum: Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Lena Metlege Diab will announce changes to immigration Express Entry categories during an address to the Canadian Club Toronto, followed by media availability.

items.title: Canada exceeds 2025 Francophone immigration target
items.sum: Canada has surpassed its immigration target for French-speaking individuals in 2025. The government states that Francophone immigration supports economic growth, cultural vitality, and addresses labour needs across the country.

items.title: Minister announces immigration initiative for Francophone communities
items.sum: The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship will hold a press conference in Moncton, New Brunswick to announce an immigration-related initiative focused on Francophone minority communities outside Quebec.

items.title: Semiahmoo First Nation receives infrastructure investment for housing
items.sum: The Semiahmoo First Nation is receiving targeted infrastructure investments to support new housing development. These investments are intended to enable more community members to live in their home community.

items.title: Parliamentary Secretary announces infrastructure improvements for Semiahmoo First Nation
items.sum: Parliamentary Secretary Ginette Lavack, along with the Chief of Semiahmoo First Nation and the local Member of Parliament, will announce improvements to community infrastructure in the First Nation.

items.title: Canada advances First Nations-led reform of child and family services
items.sum: The Government of Canada is working with First Nations to reform the First Nations Child and Family Services Program with a focus on centering children, families, and communities in service delivery.

items.title: Minister announces First Nations Child and Family Services updates
items.sum: Minister of Indigenous Services Mandy Gull-Masty will hold a press conference to provide updates on long-term reforms to the First Nations Child and Family Services Program.

items.title: Standing Buffalo Dakota Nation opens new water treatment plant
items.sum: Standing Buffalo Dakota Nation opened a new water treatment plant to provide clean water access and improve community infrastructure. The facility represents an investment in long-term water system renewal for the Nation.

items.title: New reserve established for McDowell Lake First Nation
items.sum: McDowell Lake First Nation has established the Mishi Sakahikaniing Reserve, creating a permanent land base for the community. Federal and provincial officials participated in the announcement.

items.title: Okanese First Nation opens new water treatment plant
items.sum: Okanese First Nation has opened a new water treatment plant to provide safe and clean drinking water to community members. The facility is designed to ensure long-term reliable access to water.

items.title: Budget investments announced for Chantier Naval Forillon and Exploramer
items.sum: The Minister highlighted 2025 budget investments directed toward Chantier Naval Forillon and Exploramer. The announcement contextualized these investments within broader concerns about changes to the international trading system and their effects on Canadian businesses and workers.

items.title: Minister announces Budget 2025 investments in Gaspésie region
items.sum: Minister of Indigenous Services Mandy Gull-Masty will hold a media event in Gaspé, Quebec to announce federal budget investments in the Gaspésie region.

items.title: Budget 2025 allocates funding for personal support workers
items.sum: The federal government's 2025 budget includes investment in personal support workers as part of broader economic and social spending initiatives. The budget also emphasizes community protection, housing development, and cost reduction for Canadians.

items.title: Indigenous Services Minister visits Chibougamau senior care facility
items.sum: Minister Mandy Gull-Masty will visit Manoir Providence in Chibougamau to meet with staff and seniors. During the visit, the Minister will highlight Budget 2025 measures designed to support workers.

items.title: Okanese First Nation opens early learning facility
items.sum: Okanese First Nation opened a new Aboriginal Head Start On-Reserve building designed to support early childhood development and prepare children for school. The facility serves as a community space for early learning programs.

items.title: Minister responds to Auditor General follow-up report on Indigenous programs
items.sum: Minister Gull-Masty issued a statement acknowledging the Auditor General of Canada's follow-up report examining programs for First Nations and Inuit. The statement represents the government's response to the audit findings.

items.title: Red Sucker Lake First Nation opens new school facility
items.sum: Red Sucker Lake First Nation held a grand opening for a new school. Indigenous Services Canada partnered with the First Nation to help establish the facility, which will provide education programs designed to meet students' needs and reflect Indigenous culture.

items.title: Indigenous Services Canada launches digital pilot for First Nations registration
items.sum: Indigenous Services Canada has begun the first phase of a digital pilot project to streamline the registration application process for First Nations individuals under the Indian Act. The pilot is available at in-person service locations.

items.title: Iskut Band opens new school for community youth education
items.sum: The Iskut Band held a grand opening ceremony for their new school, Łuwechōn Kots'ede'i Kime (Łuwechōn House of Learning). The school expands education opportunities for youth in the community.
